title: Early union officers and the drummer Joe Welsh
summary: They try to identify the union secretary-drummer, settling on Joe Welsh, and Humphrey recalls the first union president.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: I can't think of that a while. Anyhow, he was secretary when they first set the union up there. He was secretary for the union. Celestine was the president. His name's Joe. I knew his name, his first name was Joe.
Did he play the slide whistle too? No.
You know one of them both whistles? No.
Oh no, I know Joe Strutter.
Yeah. Uh, was this uh, I know Joe Lindsey played drums, but it couldn't be him.
No, not Joe Lindsey. I know Joe Lindsey. The only other drummer I can think of is Windy Joe Wynn.
You know Joe Wynn, but that's not him.
Yeah, well he's been going with me. He went to Penn School and kept on going. He broke up, he tried to break up the union. Joe Wynn.

See like Alfred played? Uh huh. Same type of drummer. Steady, huh? Steady drummer. Then he could play a nice violin. His father was a musician. Could draw notes man. Looked like he'd come out to print. Uh huh. Mr. Welch. Was he a trumpet player, was it that one? was it that one? I can't remember. I don't know what Joe Welson's father played, because I know he used to play with my grandfather, but I never seen him. I met his mother and his sisters, and I know when they first set the union up here, he was secretary. Salas was voted for the president. And we had good bands. T-Boy always was a good guitar player. That's Ramey, T-Boy Ramey Adams. He was playing guitar, huh?
